{{Quote|You will always be welcomed in our domed paradise.|The Duchess to [[Din Djarin]] and [[Bo-Katan Kryze]]|<ref name="Chapter 22" />}}
'''The Duchess''' was a [[Gender|female]] [[human]] who ruled over her homeworld, [[Plazir-15]], alongside her husband [[Bombardier (individual)|Bombardier]]. Their dream of transforming the [[planet]] into a paradise was threatened by the security chief [[Helgait]]'s plot to sabotage the [[Unidentified domed city|capital city's]] [[droid]] laborers with [[smuggler|smuggled]] [[NM-K reconstitutor|nano-droids]]. When the [[Mandalorian]]s [[Bo-Katan Kryze]] and [[Din Djarin]] visited the planet, the Duchess and her husband recruited them to [[Mission to Plazir-15|investigate the droid problem]], while she meanwhile formed a close and immediate bond with their young companion [[Din Grogu|Grogu]]. When the Mandalorians uncovered Helgait's scheme, the Duchess pronounced a sentence of [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] and granted honors to the pair and to Grogu.

==Biography==
===Ready to be loved===
[[File:Royal_family_of_Plazir15_MandoS3.png|thumb|left|200px|Lord Bombardier and the Duchess of Plazir-15]]
The [[Duchess]] was born into a noble family on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] of [[Plazir-15]]. Her family had ruled the planet since it was first settled. Her world suffered greatly under the rule of the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Chapter 22" /> 

After the Empire fell and the [[New Republic]] replaced it, a former Imperial [[officer]], [[Captain]] [[Bombardier (individual)|Bombardier]], was granted [[New Republic Amnesty Program|amnesty]] and assigned to help rebuild Plazir-15. As part of his program, he oversaw the rehabilitation of a large force of former Imperial and [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] [[droid]]s, which were reprogrammed to peacefully serve the citizens. While carrying out this work, Bombardier and the Duchess fell in love and were [[Marriage|wed]].<ref name="Chapter 22" />

===About time===
{{Quote|You see, it was time for our planet to move into a new age. We held direct democratic elections for the first time in our history.|The Duchess|<ref name="Chapter 22" />}}
The Duchess and Bombardier decided to enact revolutionary changes to remake their society according to their ideals. They held the first [[Democracy|democratic]] elections on the planet; while they wished to remain the [[Head of State|heads of state]], they wanted to owe their positions to the people's will, not to family lineage.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> They were duly elected and were seated as the [[Royal family of Plazir-15]]. [[Plazir-15's government]] was restructured according to principles of direct democracy and cultural pluralism.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

The new labor force of droids turned out to be sufficient to meet most of the planet's needs. Most citizens were free to stop working. The planet's [[Ugnaught]]s continued to proudly work to maintain the droids, and other organics staffed some departments of the local administration, but most citizens devoted themselves to recreation, the arts, and political participation. For their part, most of the droids were satisfied with this arrangement, because they saw work on Plazir-15 as their only alternative to the scrap heap.<ref name="Chapter 22" /> 

Meanwhile, due to Bombardier's Imperial past, the New Republic forbade Plazir-15 to have a standing military. For defense, Bombardier and the Duchess contracted a faction of [[Mandalorian warrior]]s loyal to [[Axe Woves]] to serve as [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] and [[privateer]]s. The military force was furthermore banned from entering the capital city, while city [[constable]]s had to to go unarmed.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

===All the rumors are true===
In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{MandoDate|22}}</ref> a crisis began to grow in Plazir-15 as dangerous malfunctions appeared in one droid after another. The constables could not effectively protect the citizens from rogue former [[battle droid]]s and other military robots, while the planet's Security Office, led by [[Chief of Security]] [[Helgait]], made no progress uncovering the cause of the problem. The citizens, meanwhile, refused the precautionary measure of shutting down all the droids, unwilling to interrupt their lifestyle of ease and plenty.<ref name="Chapter 22" /> 

[[Bo-Katan Kryze]] arrived on Plazir-15 hoping to convince Woves' privateers, who all were formerly of [[Bo-Katan Kryze's unit|her unit of warriors]], to rejoin her in a planned [[Conflict on Mandalore|reconquest]] of the planet [[Mandalore]]. [[Din Djarin]] and [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] accompanied her. The arrival of two unaffiliated Mandalorians gave the Duchess and Bombardier an idea for solving their problem. Since the Mandalorians were not part of any organized military force, they would be allowed inside the city; and since their weapons were integral to their culture, they would be permitted to bear them, per Plazir's principle of cultural pluralism. Thus, a loophole would allow them to deal with the malfunctioning droids.<ref name="Chapter 22" /> 

The Duchess and Bombardier had a pair of droids direct the trio into one of the city's [[hyperloop pod]]s and brought it to the room where they were enjoying a party with several guests. The Duchess was immediately drawn to Grogu. She asked to hold him; while Din Djarin thought he would be unlikely to trust a stranger, the child eagerly leapt into her arms, to her delight. Bombardier then invited the visitors to come and "see the view." Out of earshot of the other guests, he and the Duchess told the visitors about their problem and asked for help in eliminating the malfunctioning droids. In return, the couple would give Kryze their diplomatic support as she worked to gain sovereignty over Mandalore: through Axe Woves, they knew who she was and had learned all about her quest.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

===Truth hurts===
Kryze and Djarin went off into the city to confront the rogue droids and seek the cause of the malfunction. While they conducted their investigation, the Duchess, Bombardier, and their guests continued entertaining themselves with a game involving bouncing [[pill bug]]s through a series of hoops. Grogu, watching, used his growing skills in [[the Force]] to [[Telekinesis|manipulate]] the Duchess's bug through four consecutive hoops, scoring her a [[quadro-blast]].<ref name="Chapter 22" /> 

Kryze and Djarin arrived with a captured and penitent Helgait. They had discovered that smuggled [[NM-K reconstitutor|nano-droids]] were causing the droid laborers to act erratically, and they identified the chief of security as the person behind the nano-droids. He readily confessed his crime to the Duchess and asked that he might be forgiven, just as Bombardier had been forgiven for his work done for the Empire. Though wounded by his betrayal, the Duchess left open the possibility of forgiveness. In the meantime, she sentenced him to [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] on the [[Moon of Paraqaat]].<ref name="Chapter 22" /> 

The Mandalorians had fulfilled their promise, so the Duchess allowed them to go meet with Woves and his privateers. She first gave the [[Key to Plazir]] to the pair, the planet's highest honor. She then called Grogu, called for a ceremonial [[sword]], and [[Knight (noble rank)|knighted]] the child into the [[Ancient Order of Independent Regencies]]. The visitors wished the royal couple farewell and left the city to confront Woves and his privateers. Kryze challenged Woves, defeated him in combat, and renewed her claim to be the restored [[Mandalore (title)|ruler of the Mandalorian people]].<ref name="Chapter 22" />

==Personality and traits==
Born into nobility, the Duchess carried herself with charm, compassion, and grace.<ref name = "Encyclopedia" /> She formed an immediate bond with Grogu when he came to Plazir-15, despite the child's habitual mistrust of strangers. The Duchess and Captain Bombardier had a happy marriage and while she was prone to honestly mentioning when her husband was wrong, she loved him dearly and considered him to be the love of her life. The Duchess was an idealistic ruler. Despite her high station, she willingly ceded power to the people of her world, instituting radical changes to [[Plazir-15's government]] and submitting to a free election. On the other hand, she held on to a few royal prerogatives and was ready to use them. She summarily gave Commissioner Helgait a sentence of exile and handed out royal honors to the Mandalorian visitors.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

==Equipment==
The Duchess dressed in elaborate [[clothing]] befitting a royal. Her gown was made of fabrics of different colors and strings of gems. Her headdress of gems and metal shaped her long braided hair. Her wardrobe included a luminescent structure in the shape of a giant flower that could hover behind her and follow as she walked.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Duchess appeared in "[[Chapter 22: Guns for Hire]]," the sixth episode of the [[Disney+]] television series [[Star Wars: The Mandalorian|''The Mandalorian's'']] [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]],<ref name="Chapter 22" /> which was released on [[April 5]], [[2023]].<ref name="Facebook">{{Facebook|username=StarWars|url=StarWars/photos/a.236789496372962/6208851785833340|name=''[[Star Wars]]''|quote=This is the Way. Lock in your weekly #TheMandalorian nights. The season started streaming March 1 on #DisneyPlus.|archivefile=File:MandoSchedule.jpg}}</ref> She was portrayed by the musician [[Lizzo]]. Lizzo's [[List of cameos in Star Wars|cameo]], like that of [[Jack Black]], who played Bombardier, was not announced beforehand, and their appearance was meant as a surprise for viewers. Lizzo had first caught script writer [[Jon Favreau]]'s attention through her social media posts about ''The Mandalorian'', including a photo of herself in costume as Grogu. The whimsical character of the Duchess seemed suited for her, and she was contacted by the show and offered the role. Both actress and crew were entertained by the fact that the Duchess, like Lizzo, was a huge Grogu fan.<ref name="EW">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/the-mandalorian-lizzo-jack-black-star-wars-inside-story|text=The inside story of how Lizzo ended up on The Mandalorian|author=Dalton Ross|date=2023-04-08|work=Entertainment Weekly|archivedate=20250405022531}}</ref>

The character's title is not in the episode's dialogue, but it was first mentioned in the episode's caption, spelled "The Dutchess".<ref name="Chapter 22" /> [[StarWars.com]] and the [[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy|''Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] instead use the standard spelling "[[Duchess]]", and this article assumes the caption to be a misspelling.<ref name="Bounty Hunting Highlights">{{SW|url=news/the-mandalorian-chapter-22-guns-for-hire-highlights|text=Bounty Hunting Highlights: 5 of Our Favorite Moments from ''The Mandalorian'' – "Chapter 22: Guns for Hire"}}</ref><ref name="Encyclopedia" />
